problem: “I’ve run the numbers on a napkin. I need someone to run them properly.”
solution: A monthly model with a base case and a stress case, carried to break-even volume and ending in a go / no-go call in plain words. Sometimes the call is no.

problem: “The bank wants a business plan by the end of the month.”
solution: Pro forma statements and a use-of-funds table drawn from the model, with a narrative that answers underwriting questions before they come up.

problem: “We signed the lease. Now what do we register first?”
solution: A setup sequence that puts registrations and banking in the right order, so nothing stalls waiting on a document you could have filed in week one.

problem: “Next to the big firms, we look like a side project.”
solution: Positioning and a capability statement that say plainly what you do and for whom, without overstating your size. Buyers notice when you do.

problem: “Everyone could be a customer. That’s the problem.”
solution: One customer segment to win first and an offer priced to the contribution margin you need, laid out as a 90-day plan with weekly actions.

problem: “Investors keep asking about our unit economics, and we keep guessing.”
solution: A model that shows contribution margin per unit and how it moves with volume. The deck and data room checklist are then built to match it.

problem: “Some months the phone won’t stop ringing. Then it goes quiet for weeks.”
solution: Segmented target lists worked on a fixed follow-up cadence, with stage conversion reviewed on a weekly scorecard so the quiet months show up early.

problem: “Search for our trade in our own town and we’re on page three.”
solution: A complete Google Business Profile and consistent NAP across directories, then schema markup and pages written to how buyers actually search.

problem: “We post on social media because we feel like we should.”
solution: Positioning and an ideal customer profile first, then a channel plan sized to the budget, with one number per channel that says whether to keep going.

problem: “Our best clients came from referrals, and I couldn’t tell you how.”
solution: A referral-partner program with collateral each type of partner can hand to a client, and a CRM field that records who referred whom.

problem: “Half the deals in our CRM died months ago.”
solution: Pipeline stages with written exit criteria and required fields, plus a weekly CRM hygiene routine short enough that people actually do it.

problem: “Our work is good. Our brochure isn’t.”
solution: Collateral written and designed to one standard, starting with the piece your salespeople hand over most often.

problem: “If I take a week off, things stop.”
solution: SOPs for the work that repeats and decision rights written down, so most questions get answered without reaching you.

problem: “Every project runs late, and we find out at the end.”
solution: A critical path and risk register for each project, with change orders priced and signed before the extra work starts.

problem: “I spend Sunday nights on paperwork.”
solution: A back-office review of vendor terms and compliance deadlines, with renewals on one calendar and the repetitive steps automated where it pays.

problem: “We find out we had a bad month weeks after it ended.”
solution: A weekly scorecard of a few leading numbers, each with an owner, pulled from systems you already use.

problem: “New hires shadow someone for months and still ask the same questions.”
solution: An onboarding plan built on written SOPs, with a role scorecard that says what good looks like at 30 and 90 days.

problem: “Our leadership meeting is a status update nobody needs.”
solution: An operating rhythm with a fixed agenda: the scorecard first, open issues second, and decisions logged with an owner and a date.

problem: “Everyone says we should be using AI. I don’t know what for.”
solution: A workflow audit to find the repetitive intake and drafting work, then one scoped pilot with human review, measured in hours returned per week.

problem: “I tell people not to look at our website.”
solution: A fast, accessible site that passes Core Web Vitals and that your own staff can edit without calling a developer.

problem: “We type the same customer details into four different systems.”
solution: Forms wired to the CRM and the accounting system, so a record is entered once and the re-keying stops.

problem: “We pay for software I’ve never seen anyone open.”
solution: Every subscription listed with its cost and its owner. What nobody owns gets cancelled, and what stays gets set up properly.

problem: “A former employee might still have the passwords.”
solution: MFA on every account and access set by role in Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, with an offboarding checklist that removes leavers the same day.

problem: “Month-end reporting eats two days.”
solution: Data cleaned once at the source and a dashboard built on top of it, so the monthly report is a refresh instead of a project.

problem: “There’s grant money out there. We can’t tell which of it is for us.”
solution: An eligibility screen against each NOFO, then a ranked shortlist showing the deadline and cost share for every program worth pursuing.

problem: “We applied last year and got a form rejection.”
solution: A read of the reviewer comments, then a rewrite built on a logic model, with a budget that ties to every activity in the narrative.

problem: “We need two more people and can’t carry them through training.”
solution: On-the-Job Training and Work-Based Learning programs mapped to your hiring plan with the regional workforce board. OJT reimburses part of a new hire’s wages while they train.

problem: “The application asks for a UEI. What’s a UEI?”
solution: SAM.gov registration and a UEI, started first. Registration can take weeks, and federal applications can’t be submitted without it.

problem: “The RFP is eighty pages and due in three weeks.”
solution: A compliance matrix that maps every requirement to a page of the response, then the capability statement and proposal written against it.

problem: “We won the grant. Now the reporting starts.”
solution: A post-award reporting calendar, with expenses recorded on the award’s reimbursement basis so draws go through and the next application starts clean.

problem: “We need a COO. We can’t afford a COO.”
solution: A fractional operator on a monthly retainer, acting as owner of record for agreed objectives on the days each month when they matter.

problem: “This initiative has been ‘next quarter’ for a year.”
solution: An owner of record for the initiative, working to a weekly cadence with KPIs that show whether it moved.

problem: “Our operations head left last month.”
solution: Interim leadership that keeps the operating cadence running, then a written handover the permanent hire can use from the first day.

problem: “I make the big calls alone and second-guess every one.”
solution: A standing advisory session, prepared from your numbers, where the decision gets argued out before you make it.

problem: “We hired a senior leader and it didn’t work out.”
solution: Run the function fractionally first, then write the role from what it actually needed and hire into a job that has already been done once.

problem: “Sales promises things operations hears about on Monday.”
solution: A defined handoff from sales to operations, with required fields and a short weekly meeting, so commitments are seen before they come due.

problem: “I’m a clinician with a device idea and no idea what comes next.”
solution: Written user needs and design inputs first, then a prior art search and a staged roadmap with a decision gate before each round of spending.

problem: “The formulation works on paper. We haven’t made a batch yet.”
solution: Excipient review and a design of experiments, then stability testing scoped before you commit to a contract lab or CDMO.

problem: “Is this a 510(k) or a De Novo? Nobody will give us a straight answer.”
solution: Device classification and predicate device research, organized as a brief for your regulatory counsel, who makes the call and the submission.

problem: “We need a prototype and don’t know who builds these.”
solution: Contract manufacturers and material suppliers shortlisted against a written specification, with their quotes compared side by side.

problem: “We’re pre-revenue and the lab bills are real.”
solution: An SBIR Phase I and II strategy timed to your development milestones, so non-dilutive money pays for the riskiest work.

problem: “Our R&D history is in two notebooks and somebody’s inbox.”
solution: Design controls habits from day one, so the design history file is assembled from records that already exist.

problem: “The bank balance and the books haven’t matched in over a year.”
solution: The books rebuilt from bank and card statements, with each difference traced to the transaction that caused it and given a dollar figure.

problem: “We’re busy all year and the margin still isn’t there.”
solution: A three-way match on purchases and a sweep for duplicate payments and unbilled retainage receivable, with findings ranked by dollar impact.

problem: “Our CPA mentioned the R&D credit once. Nobody followed up.”
solution: A screen for the R&D credit and the Work Opportunity Tax Credit, with anything promising documented and handed to your CPA to claim.

problem: “A buyer wants three years of clean financials.”
solution: A cleaned chart of accounts with consistent cost coding, and reconciled history documented well enough for your CPA or the buyer’s accountant to rely on.

problem: “The project has been waiting on a zoning variance since spring.”
solution: Entitlements coordination that maps the requirements and who decides, keeping the process moving alongside your land-use attorney and engineer.

problem: “We’re probably eligible for HUBZone. We’ve never applied.”
solution: Certification readiness for 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB or DBE, with the eligibility file assembled before the application goes in.
